memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If anyone's bull injures someone else's bull and it dies, the two parties are to sell the live one and divide both the money and the dead animal equally. However, if it was known that the bull had the habit of goring, yet the owner did not keep it penned up, the owner must pay, animal for animal, but he can keep the dead animal." - Exodus 21:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a wonderfully balanced picture of justice. If two bulls fought and one died by pure accident, the loss was shared fairly between both owners — neither one bore the whole burden. But if an owner knew his bull was dangerous and did nothing, he alone paid the full cost. God's justice is neither harsh nor loose; it is exactly fair, weighing both the accident and the negligence.

This balance reflects the very character of God. He is perfectly just — never letting the careless off the hook, yet never crushing the innocent under blame they do not deserve. In a world where justice is so often twisted, bought, or ignored, how reassuring it is that our God gets it exactly right every time. He sees the full picture we cannot see.

And here is our comfort: this perfectly just God is also perfectly merciful. At the cross, His justice was fully satisfied and His mercy fully poured out, both at once (Rom 3:26). He did not sweep our wrong under the rug; He dealt with it in Christ. We can trust a God like this — to judge the world rightly, and to forgive us completely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I trust that God's justice is perfectly fair, even when human justice fails?
How does it comfort me that God is both perfectly just and perfectly merciful?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are perfectly just and perfectly merciful. When human fairness fails, help me rest in Your righteous judgment, and thank You that at the cross both met for me. Amen.
